description:
The brass tube over the bench rattles, coughs, and drops a canister into the tray. Inside is a bill, and under it a note.

BACK RENT, No. 9 Sprocket Row.
Four quarters at 350 Crowns.
Due: 1,400 Crowns.

"Hester left owing a year, in the middle of a job, and never came back for either. Not your fault, but your workshop now. The Counting-House sends me round every Friday until it is paid. I sent her a year of Fridays. Sorry."
Pip Tumbler

Pip carries Sprocket Row's letters and bills. Crowns are the brass coins the rats drop when you beat them.

options.label: Stick the bill on the spike above the vice. The rats' Crowns go towards it, and whatever scrap you can sell.

success.text: You push the bill onto the spike above the vice, where it can watch you work. A night of rats will not pay it; a night of rats and a good deal of scrap sold at the Counting-House window might. On Friday Pip will come up the Row and look at the spike, and say sorry again, and mean it a little less each time.

options.label: Offer to mend something for Pip, with ten pieces of Rat Scrap for parts, if Pip will take 80 Crowns off.

success.text: The canister comes back within the hour holding a carriage clock that has not struck since anyone can remember, and a note: "A clerk's. If it strikes, I can take 80 off." You take the back off, find a hairspring wound round itself like a nervous cat, and coax it straight with wire picked from ten pieces of your Rat Scrap. At six o'clock the clock strikes seven. The clerk, Pip reports, accepts this as close enough. You owe 1,320 Crowns.
